about: Residents' troubles (Docs/Design/57-changing-the-world.md, 3): what may weigh on a resident, read only from the simulation's real state, never invented. A resident carries one at a time: the first kind in `order` that holds. Each kind can be switched off (`on`). `briefing` is what the NPC Mind is told (in the second person, to the resident); `said` are the game's own answers to 'is something troubling you?' (one chosen by hash), and `saidBy` the same as a household's band says them (doc 79, Phase 8: "destitute", "poor"), where it has one; `unfinished` is the line in the hearer's unfinished business ({who}: the resident as the hearer knows them). Blanks: {coins}, {days}, {need}, {other} (a resident as the troubled one knows them), {shop}, {age}, {them} and {their} (the child's pronouns, by sex). `limits`: a solved kind rests that many days for that resident; one of a resident's troubles solved by the same wolf a season; making peace needs trust 30 from both and the three within 4 tiles; speaking for a resident needs the employer's trust 30; sponsoring an apprenticeship, the master's trust 20. Pennies (an apprenticeship's `fee`) are as written, as the catalogue's prices are. Every number is a placeholder.

short.briefing: Your trouble (true): your household has money and food for only about {days} days. Speak of it if the talk turns that way or they ask how you are. Never ask outright for money.
said: Money's tight. There's barely {days} days' food in the house, and that's if nobody falls ill.
We're getting by. Just. The larder and the purse together might see us through {days} days.

destitute: There's nothing in the house. What's there won't see out {days} days, and then it's the chapel steps.
What we earn doesn't buy enough bread. {days} days, maybe, if we're careful. Then I don't know.
poor: Money's tight. There's barely {days} days' food in the house, and that's if nobody falls ill.
We scrape by, week to week, and this week the scraping's thin. {days} days' food, and the rest is hope.

child.briefing: Your trouble (true): {other}, your child of {age}, has no trade and no master will take {them} on yet. Speak of it if the talk turns that way or they ask how you are. Never ask outright for help.
said: It's {other}. {age} years old and no trade to {their} name. Nobody's taken {them} on.
My {other} wants a trade, but no master in town has room for an apprentice.

work.briefing: Your trouble (true): you have no steady work; you get by on day labour and whatever turns up. Speak of it if the talk turns that way or they ask how you are. Never ask outright for help.
said: No steady work. I labour for the Town Works when they'll have me, and that's all.
I've no post. Day labour, odd jobs; it's no way to live.

feud.briefing: Your trouble (true): you and {other} can't stand each other, and it sours every day. Speak of it if the talk turns that way or they ask how you are.
said: There's bad blood between me and {other}, and it isn't getting better.
